rules: FAA Part 135 listing is regulatory authorization evidence and is not treated as proof of active commercial flights.

When an operator primary source reports a new Part 135 authorization before the FAA package-delivery page is updated, preserve that authorization as a separate event without adding it to the FAA-listed registry view.
FAA certificate and event timing are stored only at the precision directly stated by the canonical source; month-level evidence is not fabricated into a day-level date.

FAA NEPA findings and records of decision are environmental authorization evidence and are not treated as proof that commercial service has started or that the authorized daily maximum was actually achieved.
Capacity testing and delivery benchmarks from a research and development facility remain testing evidence and are not promoted to active commercial service.
Commercial package-delivery events require a primary source to state that operations or commercial deliveries actually began; future wording is not promoted to an operation event.
If the current FAA page does not publish a current operating area, operating_area remains null rather than inferred from historical or launch geography.
regulatory authorization, testing, supervised, commercial package delivery and commercial driverless trucking are kept distinct.
planned routes or future driverless validation are not promoted to commercial_driverless facts.
operator statements and filings are stored with their original qualifiers such as nearly, over, or more than.
